items.requirement: The legacy protocol selects health through a special suite name.
The legacy runner executes health before other deployed application suites.
Accessibility, performance, visual, API, and end-to-end suites depend on health.
The legacy health suite requests no named capability.
The legacy health suite expects another component to start the target server.
The legacy health suite does not perform browser automation.
The legacy health suite reads its settings from the serve object.
The legacy health suite defaults the serve type to static.
The legacy health suite defaults a static target to port 9999.
The legacy health suite defaults a server target to port 3000.
An explicit serve port overrides the port default.
The health path defaults to the root path.
The health request count defaults to three attempts.
The retry base delay defaults to 1000 milliseconds.
The request timeout defaults to 10000 milliseconds.
Optional smoke paths add HTTP checks after the main health request.
Optional smoke text assertions use a map keyed by smoke path.
Every health or smoke path must be an absolute local URL path.
Each smoke text key must also occur in the smoke path list.
Each expected smoke text value must be a non-empty string.
The legacy health suite sends HTTP GET requests.
The legacy health suite limits requests to localhost.
The legacy request sends an Accept header for HTML, JSON, or another response.
The legacy request aborts when its per-request timeout expires.
The legacy request reads the response body.
Any HTTP status from 200 through 299 passes the default status check.
A non-success HTTP status fails the health check after retries.
A connection failure fails the health check after retries.
The configured retry value counts the first request and all later requests.
The legacy retry delay doubles after each failed request.
The legacy health loop stops after the first successful response.
Smoke checks run sequentially after the main health check passes.
Each smoke path receives one request without an internal retry.
A non-success smoke response creates a critical finding.
A smoke connection failure creates a critical finding.
A smoke text assertion passes when the response body contains the declared text.
A successful main health request reports one passed check.
A failed main health request reports one failed check and one finding.
The result count includes the main request and every smoke path.
Result metadata records URL, status, response time, and attempt count.
A failed health or smoke assertion fails the suite gate.
An invalid health path produces an error result with a stable reason.
Invalid smoke configuration produces an error result with a stable reason.
The legacy suite logs the target, retries, failures, and successful response.
The legacy suite stores no structured report or response-body artifact.
Independent suite execution continues according to the shared dependency graph.
The replacement must not read an unbounded response body into memory.
The replacement must honor cancellation while a request or response body is active.
The replacement must validate retry, delay, timeout, and port limits before execution.
The replacement must not invert or misstate critical failure metadata for smoke failures.
